predictions: There will be no reproducible, variant-dependent TF-binding effect that explains a change in POU5F1B expression.

chains.title: TCF7L2-mediated effect at the enhancer-like element, with POU5F1B as a candidate target

links.claim: TCF7L2 is a candidate because it is expressed in HCT116 and has ChIP-seq peaks overlapping the variant there. Alt (T) is a working direction for this hypothesis, not an observed binding effect: no QBiC-SELEX result or allele-specific binding result is supplied.
The variant overlaps the pELS cCRE EH38E3858447, with DNase and H3K27ac signal among ENCODE biosamples; the supplied maxima do not establish activity of this element in HCT116.

POU5F1B is a plausible, not established, target: T is associated with higher POU5F1B expression in transverse colon, and POU5F1B has the strongest L2G score in the listed sets, but the L2G evidence is predominantly prostate-related and no evidence directly connects this cCRE to the gene.
TCF7L2 occupancy overlapping the variant is reported in HCT116; this supports occupancy in this cell line, not an allele-specific effect.

T is reported as the risk allele in a colorectal-cancer association, although other listed colorectal or colon traits report G as the effect allele. POU5F1B has some gene-level colorectal-cancer support, but its cited functional literature concerns a different regulatory mechanism; a TCF7L2-mediated route from this variant to disease is unproven.

predictions: A controlled comparison of G and T will show a reproducible TCF7L2-binding difference at this sequence, with the working prediction that T binds more strongly.
If this chain is correct, disrupting TCF7L2 or the variant-containing element will alter POU5F1B expression in an appropriate colorectal context.
falsified_if: A sensitive controlled assay finds no G-versus-T difference in TCF7L2 binding, and TCF7L2 or element perturbation does not affect POU5F1B expression.
